title: PitchBook API Review: Can You Build on It? [2026]
snippet:
The answer is complicated. PitchBook does offer a [RESTful JSON API](https://pitchbook.com/products/direct-access-data/api) covering all of its core entity types, but the API is an enterprise add-on that requires a separate contract on top of an existing platform subscription. The developer documentation is not publicly accessible. There are no published rate limits, no public endpoint reference, no official SDKs, and no self-serve signup.

| **Attribute** | **Detail** |
|---|---|
| **API type** | REST over HTTPS, JSON responses |
| **Authentication** | API key or token-based (specific mechanism not publicly documented) |
| **Base URL** | Not publicly documented |
| **Rate limits** | Not publicly documented |
| **Pricing / access** | Enterprise add-on requiring a [separate contract](https://pitchbook.com/help/PitchBook-api) on top of a PitchBook platform subscription; quote-only |
| **SDKs** | None |
| **Webhooks** | Not supported |
| **Documentation** | Behind platform authentication; not publicly accessible. [Help page overview](https://pitchbook.com/help/PitchBook-api) available |

Getting API access is not a self-serve process. The API belongs to **PitchBook's** [Direct Data](https://pitchbook.com/products/direct-access-data) product line, and access requires a [standalone contract](https://pitchbook.com/help/PitchBook-api) separate from a standard platform subscription. There is no developer portal, no API key generator in the dashboard, and no free-trial API access.

Developer support routes through the assigned account team and Direct Data specialists. There is no public developer forum, community channel, or self-serve support path.

**PitchBook** does not publish API or Data Feed pricing. Both are [premium add-ons](https://pitchbook.com/pricing) to the core platform subscription, and each requires a separate contract. The base PitchBook platform is required before Direct Data can be contracted, which means API access requires at minimum two separate agreements: the platform subscription and the Direct Data contract.
Cost varies by seat count and firm type; all Direct Data pricing is quote-only and negotiated through PitchBook's Direct Data team. No per-call metering, credit-pack costs, or minimum plan tiers appear anywhere on the public site. title: PitchBook integration
snippet:
Prerequisites
- A [PitchBook](https://pitchbook.com/) subscription with **API access** enabled — API access is a paid, contract-gated add-on with no free tier
- A PitchBook API key issued to your organization
- A positive **API credit balance** — PitchBook charges credits per request, and calls fail with `402 Payment Required` when the balance runs out. Ask your PitchBook account manager to add credits.

PitchBook API keys are provisioned as part of a paid API add-on rather than generated self-serve. Contact your PitchBook account manager (or your organization's PitchBook administrator) to enable API access and issue an API key for your account.

title: PitchBook API: Access, Pricing, and What You Get
snippet:
PitchBook doesn’t sell its API as a standalone product with a price tag. It’s a premium add-on layered on top of a paid platform subscription. Access only comes through a separate contract with PitchBook’s Direct Data team. There’s no public price list for it anywhere, not even on PitchBook’s own site. This guide walks through what it costs, what it actually gives you, and whether your team needs it.

There’s no developer signup page. There’s no “generate an API key” button in the dashboard. You can’t start testing without a sales conversation first. Access works differently depending on where you’re starting from:
- **Existing PitchBook platform customers** go to *My PitchBook → Plugins & Apps → PitchBook API* inside the platform. That routes a request to the Direct Data team.
- **New customers** contact the Direct Data team directly. API access then gets negotiated alongside a platform subscription.
Either way, credentials only arrive after a contract is signed — an API key or token. A sandbox environment exists for pre-production testing once you’re in the process. It gives developers a space to practice calls before

This is the part that catches developers off guard. It’s worth setting expectations before you sign anything:
- **No public rate limits.** Call-volume caps and burst limits aren’t published anywhere. Constraints get set per contract with the Direct Data team, so you can’t plan integration capacity until after the deal is signed.
- **No official SDKs.** The API works with any standard HTTP client, but no maintained client library exists in any language. Your team owns the full integration layer: authentication, request handling, pagination, retries, error handling.
- **Documentation stays private.** The API guide and endpoint reference sit behind platform authentication, visible only to contracted clients. There’s no public OpenAPI spec and no interactive explorer.
- **No webhooks.** Real-time updates mean polling the API yourself. There’s no event-driven or push-notification pattern. Scheduled delivery is what the Data Feed handles, not the API.
- **A sandbox does exist.** Once you’re in the process, PitchBook provides a test environment for practicing call structure before going live. The Direct Data team supports onboarding during this phase.
